L75: Further, CSS allows the user agent to choose when to actually load a font; if a font face isn’t currently used by anything on a page, most user agents will not download its associated file. This means that later use of the font face will incur a delay as the user agent finally notices a usage and begins downloading and parsing the font file.
L76: This specification defines a scripting interface to font faces in CSS, allowing font faces to be easily created (via the `cite54†FontFace ` interface) and loaded from script (via cite33†document.fonts ). It also provides methods to track the loading status of an individual font, or of all the fonts on an entire page.
L77: Several things in this spec use normal ES objects to define behavior, such as various things using Promises internally, and FontFaceSet using a Set internally. I believe the intention here is that these objects (and their prototype chains) are pristine, unaffected by anything the author has done. Is this a good intention? If so, how should I indicate this in the spec?

L172: All `cite54†FontFace ` objects contain an internal `[[FontStatusPromise]]` slot, which tracks the status of the font. It starts out pending, and fulfills or rejects when the font is successfully loaded and parsed, or hits an error.
L173: All `cite54†FontFace ` objects also contain internal `[[Urls]]` and `[[Data]]` slots, of which one is `null` and the other is not `null` (the non-null one is set by the constructor, based on which data is passed in).
L174: ### 2.1. The Constructor
L175: 
L176: A `cite54†FontFace ` can be constructed either from a URL pointing to a font face file, or from a `cite62†BufferSource†webidl.spec.whatwg.org ` containing the binary representation of a font face.
L177: 
L178: When the `FontFace(family, source, descriptors)` method is called, execute these steps:
L179:   1. Let `font face` be a fresh `cite54†FontFace ` object. Set `font face’s` `cite76†status ` attribute to `"unloaded"`, Set its internal `cite94†[[FontStatusPromise]] ` slot to a fresh pending `cite55†Promise†webidl.spec.whatwg.org ` object.
L180: cite89†Parse the `cite95†family ` argument, and the members of the `cite96†descriptors ` argument, according to the grammars of the corresponding descriptors of the CSS cite53†@font-face rule. If the `cite97†source ` argument is a `cite59†CSSOMString `, parse it according to the grammar of the CSS src descriptor of the @font-face rule.
L181: If any of them fail to parse correctly, reject `font face’s` `cite94†[[FontStatusPromise]] ` with a DOMException named "SyntaxError", set `font face’s` corresponding attributes to the empty string, and set `font face’s` `cite76†status ` attribute to "error". Otherwise, set `font face’s` corresponding attributes to the serialization of the parsed values.
L182: Note: Note that this means that passing a naked url as the source argument, like `"http://example.com/myFont.woff"`, won’t work - it needs to be at least wrapped in a cite98†url() function, like `"url(http://example.com/myFont.woff)"`. In return for this inconvenience, you get to specify multiple fallbacks, specify the type of font each fallback is, and refer to local fonts easily.

L215: ### 2.2. The `load()` method
L216: 
L217: The `cite93†load() ` method of `cite54†FontFace ` forces a url-based font face to request its font data and load. For fonts constructed from a buffer source, or fonts that are already loading or loaded, it does nothing.
L218: 
L219: When the `load()` method is called, execute these steps:
L220:   1. Let `font face` be the `cite54†FontFace ` object on which this method was called.
L221:   2. If `font face’s` `cite99†[[Urls]] ` slot is `null`, or its `cite76†status ` attribute is anything other than `"unloaded"`, return `font face’s` `cite94†[[FontStatusPromise]] ` and abort these steps.
L222:   3. Otherwise, set `font face’s` `cite76†status ` attribute to "loading", return `font face’s` `cite94†[[FontStatusPromise]] `, and continue executing the rest of this algorithm asynchronously.
L223:   4. Using the value of `font face’s` `cite99†[[Urls]] ` slot, attempt to load a font as defined in cite107†[CSS-FONTS-3] , as if it was the value of a cite53†@font-face rule’s src descriptor.
L224:   5. When the load operation completes, successfully or not, queue a task to run the following steps synchronously:
L225:     1. If the attempt to load fails, reject `font face’s` `cite94†[[FontStatusPromise]] ` with a DOMException whose name is "NetworkError" and set `font face’s` `cite76†status ` attribute to "error".
